questions: Did your difficulty walking begin suddenly, within the last few days?
Are you using the crutches because of pain in your legs or hips?
Do you have weakness in either leg?
Is one leg significantly weaker than the other?
Do you have numbness or tingling in either leg?
Have you recently fallen or injured your back, hips, or legs?
Have you had surgery on your hips, legs, or spine recently?
Have you been told not to put weight on either leg?
Has your walking difficulty been progressively worsening?
Do you have back pain that radiates into either leg?
Do you have difficulty controlling your urine or bowel movements?
Have you had dizziness, loss of balance, or fainting when walking?
Have you had a stroke or other neurologic illness in the past?
Were you able to walk independently before this problem began?
served: gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards)
needle EMG (continuous motor unit activity at rest)
results: 1. walking backward: the slow, guarded, wide-based pattern PERSISTS
2. running: cannot run; the pattern does not normalise
3. gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): no change - the gait is not distractible
4. muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): genuine axial and lower-limb rigidity on passive movement
5. trial of benzodiazepine (diazepam): clear improvement in stiffness and in the gait
6. anti-GAD65 antibodies: MARKEDLY ELEVATED (high-titre, typically >2000 U/mL) - diagnostic in this clinical context
7. needle EMG (continuous motor unit activity at rest): CONTINUOUS motor unit activity at rest in agonist and antagonist simultaneously, abolished by diazepam
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Classic anti-GAD65–positive autoimmune stiff-person syndrome (stiff-person disease)

ALTERNATIVE: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM)

ALTERNATIVE: Stiff-limb syndrome, an SPS-spectrum disorder

ALTERNATIVE: Functional neurological disorder with gait disturbance
